parts.problem_md:
Do you think the profitability of Izaak’s fish restaurant has improved since last year? Justify your answer using appropriate ratios.

> **[case-study]**
> Izaak owns a small fish restaurant. He employs two chefs (cooks) and three workers who serve in the restaurant.
> 
> Izaak has been trying to increase added value to improve profits. Izaak has been looking at the financial performance of his business. An extract is shown in the table below. Izaak has received a number of complaints about food and service. He knows he must improve quality but cannot decide on the best way to do this.
> 
> |   | Last year | Current year |
> |---|---|---|
> | Revenue | **X** | 300 |
> | Cost of sales | 180 | 150 |
> | Gross profit | 120 | 150 |
> | Expenses | 90 | **Y** |
> | Profit | 30 | 15 |
parts.solution_md:
Izaak's fish restaurant's profitability has not improved **[K] **since last year. While the gross profit margin has increased from 40% to 50% **[Ap]**, the overall profit margin has decreased from 10% to 5%, indicating less control over expenses **[An]**

However, the increase in gross profit margin suggests Izaak is managing his food costs better **[K]**. However, the significant drop in profit margin indicates that expenses have increased substantially, outweighing the improvement in gross profit. This could be due to higher cooking equipment costs **[Ap]**, rent, or other restaurant overheads **[An]**

**Calculation steps**

To calculate the gross profit margin, divide gross profit by revenue, then multiply the outcome by 100

Last year   $= \frac{120}{300} \times 100 

= 40 \%$

Current year    $= \frac{150}{300} \times 100 

= 50 \%$

To calculate the profit margin, divide profit by revenue, then multiply the outcome by 100

Last year   $= \frac{30}{300} \times 100 

= 10 \%$

Current year  $= \frac{15}{300} \times 100 

= 5 \%$

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - You are writing a mini-argument with a decision
> 
>   - Give one relevant reason to support your view → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this reason helps the business (cause-effect chain) →  1 An mark
>   - Give a different possible reason or viewpoint → 1 K mark
>   - Explain why this could also help the business → 1 An mark
>   - Make a decision — which argument is stronger or more important overall? → up to 2 E marks
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Answers might include:
> 
>   - Gross profit margin improved (1) from 40% to 50% (1) showing better  control of variable costs. However, profit margin down (1) from 10% to 5% (1) shows less control of expenses.
> - Justification might include:
> 
>   - The business has been less successful at making profit from its sales which means overall profitability has fallen rather than improved. (2)
> - Relevant calculations are:
> 
>   - Profit Margin: 10% in 2015, 5% in 2016
>   - Gross Profit Margin: 40% in 2015, 50% in 2016
> - Other appropriate responses should also be credited

- A measure of how effectively a business converts sales revenue** [1]** into profit **[1]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> Don't confuse profitability with profit, which is the surplus of revenue left over after all costs have been paid

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Knowledge 2
> 
>   - Give a clearly-stated, valid definition to achieve both knowledge [K] marks
>   - 2 marks for a full definition, 1 mark for a partial definition
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Profitability is a measure of how effectively a business converts sales revenue [K] into profit [K]
> 
>   - OR, The ability of a business to generate profit [K] from its income over a period of time [K]
>   - OR, An indicator of how much profit a business makes in relation to revenue, assets or capital employed [K]
> - Partial definition: The ability of a business to make a profit [K]
> 
>   - OR, How well a business turns revenue into earnings [K]

parts.problem_md:
Calculate Kemala's gross profit margin in 2021.

Show your workings.

> **[case-study]**
> Kemala makes high-quality beauty products. Demand for her best-selling hand cream is price inelastic. She advertises her products in specialist beauty magazines. Kemala is analysing her income statement. An extract is shown in the below table. She said: ‘When I started my business, I did not understand why cash is important’.
> 
> | **Extract from Kemala’s income statement 2021 (\$000)** |   |
> |---|---|
> | Revenue | 480 |
> | Gross profit | 192 |
> | Profit for the year | 72 |
parts.solution_md:
**40%** **[2]**

**Calculation steps**

Divide gross profit by revenue

$= \$ 192 , 000 \div \$ 480 , 000

= 0.40$    **[1]**

Multiply the outcome by 100 to calculate the percentage

$= 0.40 \times 100

= 40 \%$    **[1]**

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

{align=center} **The BB Health Spa (BB)**

Bethany owns The BB Health Spa in Main City in country X. Economic growth has been high for the last few years. The government of country X wants this growth to continue so it has reduced income tax. However, it is also worried about inflation becoming a problem so it has increased interest rates.

The BB Health Spa is very busy and Bethany is considering taking on a partner to help manage the business and give her more free time. However, she has been a sole trader for 10 years and wants the business to stay small.

The customers of The BB Health Spa are people of all ages who are interested in their health. Bethany employs two qualified workers to provide the treatments for customers. Bethany herself also provides customers with treatments. In addition, she does all the administration such as ordering inventory, accounts and paying invoices when the spa is closed.

The BB Health Spa still uses the original treatment equipment which was purchased when the business started. Some spas nearby have the latest equipment but these spas charge much higher prices than The BB Health Spa. Bethany records all the financial transactions by filling in accounts books by hand. This takes her a long time. Customers book appointments using the telephone and Bethany later telephones them to remind them when an appointment is due.

{align=center} **Appendix 1**

{align=center} **Advert for treatments at The BB Health Spa**

{align=center} 

{align=center} **Appendix 2 **

{align=center} **Weekly forecasts for two possible additional services**

|   | Steam room | Hair cuts |
| --- | :---: | :---: |
| Additional customers | 200 | 50 |
|   |   |   |
| Average price charged per customer | \$5 | \$25 |
| Wages | \$60 | \$400 |
| Cost of sales | \$40 | \$125 |
| Lease of equipment | \$400 | \$175 |

{align=center} 

{align=center} **Appendix 3**

**Daily News **

{align=right} **September**

{align=center} **New equipment now available in many health spas to make skin look younger**

There have been a number of changes in technology for health spas which allow the treatments to be much more effective in making skin look younger. Many people are keen to try these treatments using the latest equipment to get younger looking skin. This equipment is very expensive for health spas to buy or lease.

The news of these treatments has appeared on social media sites and on mobile phone Apps leading to higher demand. ‘Some customers will pay high prices for such treatments’, said a local health spa owner who is keen to promote his health spa as being one of the first to use the new equipment.

There have also been developments in software which make customer bookings and accounts much easier, quicker and with fewer mistakes. Automatic text (sms) messages are used to remind customers of their appointments – so no need to miss an appointment again.

Look out for these changes in health spas near you!

Consider the weekly forecasts in Appendix 2 for the two additional services Bethany could choose:

- hair cuts
- steam room.

Which additional service should Bethany choose to offer? Include a calculation of profit for the two services to justify your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/0450-01-specimen-2020-paper-2-insert-cie-igcse-business---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
The steam room option aligns with BB's existing services like sports therapies and yoga, and would attract 200 weekly customers, significantly increasing foot traffic. Its \$5 fee is accessible and matches BB's pricing strategy. The profit margin is high at 50% (\$500 profit from \$1000 revenue), and needs less specialised skills to operate, making staffing easier for Bethany

However, it has a higher equipment lease cost of \$400 per week compared to \$175 for hair cuts. Its installation might disrupt the spa's operations and there's a risk that not all 200 projected customers will use the service regularly, potentially affecting the forecasted revenue

The haircut option would generate more weekly profit (\$550 compared to \$500 for the steam room). It could attract new clients who might then use other spa services. The higher price of \$25 could be seen as adding a premium service to BB's range

However, haircuts would only attract 50 weekly customers, limiting foot traffic increase. The profit margin is lower at 44% (\$550 profit from \$1250 revenue), and it requires more specialised skills, which could complicate staffing and management for Bethany

Bethany should choose the steam room option. It aligns with BB's existing services and matches Bethany's wish to keep BB small and manageable. While haircuts offer slightly higher absolute profit, the steam room's higher profit margin, better fit with BB's brand and has the potential to attract more customers. These factors make it the better choice for sustainable growth and profitability

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the problem
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
> - Add a final Evaluation (E):
> 
>   - Decide which problem is easiest/hardest to overcome
>   - Justify your choice
>   - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Calculation steps**
> 
> Steam room
> 
> `Revenue = 200 customers x $ 5 = $ 1 , 000 > Costs = $ 60 + $ 40 + $ 400 = $ 500 > Profit = $ 1 , 000 - $ 500 = $ 500`
> 
> Hair cuts
> 
> `Revenue = 50 customers x $ 25 = $ 1 , 250 > Costs = $ 400 + $ 125 + $ 175 = $ 700 > Profit = $ 1 , 250 - $ 700 = $ 550`
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Steam room**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Price \$20 lower → attracts 150 more customers → higher volume
>     - Profit \$500 → PM 50% → strong margin per sale
>     - GPM 96% → minimal cost of sales → high profitability
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Revenue \$1000 vs \$1250 for hair cuts → lower total income
>     - Gross profit \$960 vs \$1125 for hair cuts → smaller absolute GP
>     - Profit \$500 vs \$550 for hair cuts → \$50 less cash profit
> - **Hair cuts**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Revenue \$1250 → \$250 more than steam room
>     - Profit \$550 → \$50 more than steam room
>     - Gross profit \$1125 → \$165 more than steam room
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - PM 44% vs 50% for steam room → lower margin per sale
>     - GPM 90% vs 96% for steam room → higher cost of sales
> - **Conclusion**
> 
>   - Hair cuts: deliver higher revenue and absolute profit → better for cash generation
>   - Steam room: offers superior profit and gross margins → better for overall efficiency
>   - The decision hinges on prioritising total profit (hair cuts) vs profitability ratios (steam room)
>   - Combining both services could balance volume growth with strong margins

**Extract:**

**Cherished Chocolates (CC)**

CC is a public limited company. It employs 4000 workers in country X and many are members of a trade union. CC has manufactured chocolate bars in country X for 50 years. It imports most of its raw materials, such as cocoa beans. Over the last 10 years CC has expanded and now sells in other countries. Many of these countries have no trade restrictions. The Directors of CC know that globalisation has opportunities and threats for CC. 

CC produces a number of brands of chocolate bars, such as Tiabar, in country X. Its most popular chocolate bar, Choco, has the highest market share. The total market for chocolate bars is no longer growing in country X. CC plans to reduce the number of brands it sells in country X. It has to decide which of the two brands shown in Appendix 1 to stop selling. 

NM operates in country Z and sells its own brands of chocolate bars, including Nuttybar. NM employs 500 workers. In country Z chocolate bars are distributed through small retail outlets. The wage rates in country Z are lower than in country X. However, incomes in country Z are starting to rise. 

The Directors of CC are planning to take over NM to expand into this market rather than setting up a factory. The takeover will cost \$35 million, some of which will be financed by a bank loan. The shareholders of NM are being offered CC shares in exchange for NM shares. 

The Directors of CC know there might be diseconomies of scale after the takeover. They also have to decide who will be the Operations Manager for NM’s factory in country Z. They could keep NM’s existing Operations Manager or move CC’s Operations Manager from country X. Information about the two managers is shown in Appendix 2.

{align=center} **Appendix 1 **

{align=center} **The product life cycles of two of CC’s brands of chocolate bars in country X**

**Option 1 – stop producing Tiabar **

A brand aimed at young children which is a new target market for CC. The market research at the development stage showed positive results from test marketing and sales have been growing steadily. There are many multinational chocolate bar companies targeting this age group. 

**Option 2 – stop producing Choco** 

The market leader in country X. It is a well established brand targeting adults. Sales are high but have not been increasing for several years. No new competitors have entered this market in the last two years.

{align=center} **Appendix 2**

{align=center} **Information about the two Operations Managers for NM’s factory in country Z**

|   | **Samuel ****CC’s Operations Manager** | **Ritesh ****NM’s Operations Manager** |
| --- | :---: | :---: |
| **Qualifications/Skills** | 8 IGCSEs On-the-job training in the production of chocolate bars | 5 IGCSEs and 2 A levels Degree in Business Management |
| **Experience** | 10 years as the Operations Manager for CC Worked for CC for 20 years and knows the production and warehouse storage requirements for all of its brandsHas links with all CC’s suppliers of high-quality ingredients such as cocoa beans and milk | 2 years as the Operations Manager for NM Purchased all the ingredients, including nuts, for NM’s productsPreviously worked for 5 years for a chocolate bar manufacturing business in country Z Worked for 5 years for a small retailer in country Z |

{align=center} 

{align=center} **Appendix 3 **

{align=center} **Selected information from the financial statements for CC and NM for 2021**

{align=center} 

|   | **CC** | **NM** |
| --- | :---: | :---: |
| **Long-term bank loan** | \$10m | \$5m |
| **Total shareholders’ equity** | \$200m | \$30m |
| **Current ratio** | 2 | 1 |
| **Acid test ratio** | 1.2 | 0.33 |
|   |   |   |
| **Profit for the year** | \$42m | \$3.5m |
| **Profit margin** | 25% | 15% |
| **Return on Capital Employed (ROCE)** | 20% | 10% |

Using Appendix 3 and other information, consider how the financial statements might be useful to the following **three **stakeholder groups.

- NM’s shareholders
- CC’s managers
- CC’s bank manager

Which stakeholder group will find the financial information most useful? Justify your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2022-paper-22-case-study-v2--new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
NM's shareholders can use the statements to decide whether to accept CC shares. The data shows CC is more profitable, with a profit of \$42m compared to NM's \$3.5m **[Ap]**. CC also has a higher profit margin of 25% versus NM's 15%, meaning CC keeps more of each dollar of sales as profit **[An]**. The return on capital employed (ROCE) of 20% for CC, double NM's 10% **[Ap]**, indicates CC generates better returns for shareholders, suggesting NM shareholders could benefit financially from the takeover **[An]**

CC's managers can use the statements to identify areas for improvement at NM. Its lower profit margin and ROCE show potential to increase efficiency. The acid test ratio of 0.33 for NM versus 1.2 for CC **[Ap]** indicates NM may be holding too much inventory, which CC's managers could address to boost profitability and liquidity **[An]**

CC's bank manager will examine the statements to assess CC's ability to repay the \$35m loan **[Ap] **for the takeover. CC's healthy profit of \$42m and higher liquidity ratios suggest it can comfortably make repayments on additional debt **[An]**

NM's shareholders will find the information most useful **[E]**. It directly impacts their decision to accept CC's offer and exchange their shares **[Ap]**. CC's managers would need more data to plan improvements after the takeover **[E]**. The bank manager would require cash flow forecasts to assess whether the loan can be repaid **[E]**. Therefore, as the financial statements affect NM shareholders' immediate decision-making, they will find this information most valuable **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the problem
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
> - Add a final Evaluation (E):
> 
>   - Decide which problem is easiest/hardest to overcome
>   - Justify your choice
>   - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **NM’s shareholders**
> 
>   - CC’s profit of \$42 m far exceeds NM’s \$3.5 m → signals higher potential dividends if the takeover succeeds
>   - CC’s ROCE is 10 % higher → suggests better returns for shareholders post-acquisition
>   - CC’s current ratio of 3 and acid-test of 2 contrast with NM’s ratios of 1 and < 1 → CC’s stronger liquidity makes the combined business more secure
>   - CC’s shareholders’ equity of \$200 m vs NM’s \$30 m → CC is a larger, more stable company to invest in
> - **CC’s managers**
> 
>   - CC’s 25 % profit margin vs NM’s 15 % → CC’s cost controls can be shared to boost NM’s efficiency
>   - NM’s high inventory and low acid-test (0.33) highlight working-capital issues → CC’s managers can streamline NM’s inventory and cut warehousing costs
>   - NM’s existing base in country Z and distribution network → enables CC to expand its brands quickly using NM’s local channels
> - **CC’s bank manager**
> 
>   - CC already services a \$10 m loan and seeks \$35 m more for the takeover → manageable relative to CC’s \$200 m equity
>   - CC’s \$42 m profit and NM’s \$3.5 m profit support loan repayment capacity → reassures the bank on credit risk
> - **Conclusion**
> 
>   - NM’s shareholders need profit, ROCE and liquidity comparisons to judge the takeover’s value and dividend prospects
>   - CC’s managers focus on margin and working-capital metrics to plan efficiency improvements and leverage NM’s market presence
>   - CC’s bank manager looks at profit levels and equity size to ensure the additional borrowing for the takeover is safely repayable

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

{align=center} **Cell Covers (CC) **

Aisha worked for several years for a company that repairs mobile (cell) phones in country Z. She had always wanted to be her own boss and decided to leave her job to set up CC to produce covers for mobile phones. She went into partnership with her brother, Aruna. He worked as an Operations Manager for a company producing children’s clothes. 

The sources of finance for the business were \$10 000 of savings from each partner and a bank loan of \$10 000. CC was also given a government grant to help the new business get started. CC leased a factory, bought some equipment and had to pay some expenses before the business had regular cash inflows. 

CC’s current product is a range of standardised phone covers which are sold in the mass market. These are sold using a competitive pricing method through mobile phone shops. CC employs 10 skilled production workers who are paid just above the legal minimum wage. These workers have been trained how to operate the equipment and work as a team on the production line. During the production process there is a lot of waste plastic produced and CC sends this to landfill sites. The business has just completed its second year of trading. 

CC is about to launch a new range of individual personalised phone covers. It will need to recruit 2 additional production workers. Aruna knows that the marketing mix for this new product may have to be different to the marketing mix used for the standardised products. The new product will be aimed at a niche market of high income consumers between the ages of 18 to 25. There are few other competitors in this market at present. 

{align=center} **Appendix 1 **

{align=center} **Newspaper article in Main News **

Country Z has been in a recession but the economy is now growing rapidly and unemployment is falling. With higher incomes the majority of people now own a mobile phone. This makes communication easier. Mobile banking is becoming more popular and it is used by a large percentage of the population.

{align=center} **Appendix 2 **

{align=center} **Advertisement for CC’s standardised mobile phone covers**

Do you want to protect your phone from damage? Then buy a phone cover from CC. Your phone will never be damaged if you use one of our high quality covers!! 

We offer a range of standardised covers at competitive prices. The CC range has many different colours and designs so you will stand out from the crowd.

{align=center} **Appendix 3 **

{align=center} **Summary of CC’s financial information from the end of the second year of trading (\$)**

| Revenue | 800 000 |
| --- | ---: |
| Cost of sales | 400 000 |
| Gross profit | 400 000 |
| Expenses | 250 000 |
| Profit | 150 000 |
| Current Assets | 20 000 |
| of which: Inventory | 5 000 |
| Current liabilities | 15 000 |

Using the data in Appendix 3, calculate the following ratios for CC:

- Gross profit margin
- Profit margin
- Current ratio
- Acid test ratio

Show your workings.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/09/nov-2020-paper-22-case-study-v2---new.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
**Gross profit margin = 50%** **[2]**

**Profit margin = 18.75% ****[2]**

**Current ratio = 1.33** **[2]**

**Acid test ratio = 1 ****[2]**

**Calculation steps**

Calculate the gross profit margin by dividing gross profit by revenue, then multiplying the outcome by 100

$\mathrm{Gross} \mathrm{profit} \mathrm{margin}-\frac{\mathrm{Gross} \mathrm{profit}}{\mathrm{Revenue}}\times100$    **[1]**

$= \frac{\$ 400 , 000}{\$ 800 , 000} \times 100

= 50 \%$    **[1]**

Calculate the profit margin by dividing profit by revenue, then multiplying the outcome by 100

$\mathrm{Profit} \mathrm{margin}-\frac{\mathrm{Profit}}{\mathrm{Revenue}}\times100$    **[1]**

$= \frac{\$ 150 , 000}{\$ 800 , 000} \times 100

= 18.75 \%$    **[1]**

Calculate the current ratio by dividing current assets by current liabilities

$\mathrm{Current} \mathrm{ratio}=\frac{\mathrm{Current} \mathrm{assets}}{\mathrm{Current} \mathrm{liabilities}}$    **[1]**

$= \$ 20 , 000 \div \$ 15 , 000

= 1.33$    **[1]**

Calculate the acid test ratio by subtracting inventory from current assets, then dividing the outcome by current liabilities

$\text{Acid} \text{test} \text{ratio} = \frac{ ( \text{Current} \text{assets} - \text{Inventory} )}{Current liabilities}$    **[1]**

$= ( \$ 20 , 000 - \$ 5 , 000 ) \div \$ 15 , 000

= 1.00$     **[1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> - Show your workings
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - Award 1 mark for each correct formula (maximum of four)
> - gross profit/revenue × 100 (1)
> - profit/revenue × 100 (1)
> - current assets/current liabilities (1)
> - current assets – inventory/current liabilities (1)
> 
> OR
> 
> - 1 mark for use of correct formula + 1 mark for correct answer (4 × 2 marks) \$400 000/\$800 000 × 100 (1) = 50% (1)
> - \$150 000/\$800 000 × 100 (1) = 18.75% (1)
> - \$20 000/\$15 000 (1) = 1.33 or 4:3 (1)
> - \$15 000/\$15 000 (1) = 1 (1)

Explain **one **way each of the following stakeholder groups might use VCG’s accounts:

- Shareholders

> **[case-study]**
> VCG manufactures high-quality briefcases and travel bags. VCG has 50 skilled production workers in its factory. VCG is planning to expand by building a second factory. Different locations are being considered. The Managing Director is reviewing VCG’s financial statements. An extract is shown in the below table. Both internal and external stakeholder groups of VCG are interested in this information.
> 
> | **Extract from VCG’s 2021 financial statements (\$)** |   |
> |---|---|
> | Revenue | 2 000 000 |
> | Current assets | 300 000 |
